title: Classed governance evidence record, v1
description: One governance evidence record about ONE artifact on ONE platform. The record's CLASS is a required, first-class field: upstream-base, foundry-child, staged-candidate or published-artifact. A class is never inferred and never substitutes for another. The defect this schema exists for: an upstream-base scan of php:8.4 (241 CRITICAL/HIGH, 170 of them linux-libc-dev) was reported as php-fpm/8.4 child evidence (47 CRITICAL/HIGH, 0 linux-libc-dev). The child Dockerfile runs `apt-get purge -y --auto-remove`, so linux-libc-dev is not installed in the child at all — the base record describes a DIFFERENT ARTIFACT's inventory and can neither confirm nor deny anything about what Foundry ships. Every field below exists so that an evidence record cannot be silently reused across a class, digest, platform, image version or source revision boundary.

evidence_class.description: The artifact class this record describes. REQUIRED and never defaulted. policies/evidence-classes.yaml states what each class may and may not establish.

child_key.description: Canonical identity, `<family>/<version>/<platform>`, as produced by child_key() in scripts/lib/common.sh. This is the ONE identity derivation in the repository; a second one would let two spellings of the same child diverge. Absent for upstream-base records, which are not Foundry children.

image_digest.description: IMMUTABLE manifest digest. A mutable tag is not an identity: the bytes behind it can change after the evidence is written, which is exactly how evidence outlives the artifact it described. There is deliberately no `tag` alternative.

platform.description: linux/<arch>. Evidence is per-platform: an amd64 scan says nothing about the arm64 child, which has a different digest and a different installed inventory.

image_family.description: php-fpm, php-cli, php-worker, php-frankenphp, nginx, caddy — or, for upstream-base, the upstream repository name.

image_version.description: The image family's selector: a PHP minor such as 8.3 / 8.4, or `prod` for the versionless edge images. 8.3 evidence must never satisfy an 8.4 requirement.

source_revision.description: The Foundry revision the artifact was built from. Evidence is bound to it: a later commit needs its own evidence.

build_input_digest.description: Digest of the Dockerfile / build context that produced the artifact. Two artifacts from the same revision but a different context are different artifacts.

build_completed.description: Did the build reach completion. A build that did not complete cannot emit foundry-child (or any later) evidence: a partial image's installed inventory is undefined. Enforced in policies/evidence-classes.yaml via requires_build_completion.

scanner_identity.description: The scanner image pinned by digest. A scanner referenced by tag can be swapped underneath the evidence.

vulnerability_db_identity.description: The FROZEN vulnerability database snapshot the scan was judged against. Findings are only comparable within one snapshot; two records from different snapshots differ for database reasons that are not artifact reasons.

package_inventory_source.description: Where the installed-package list came from. THE 241-vs-47 FIELD: `image-base` inventories describe the upstream base, `image-child` inventories describe what Foundry ships, and they are not the same list.

parent.description: Provenance: the record this artifact descends from. `null` ONLY for upstream-base, which by definition has no Foundry parent. Every other class must name its parent's class and immutable digest, so a child can be traced to the exact base bytes it was built on.

severity_counts.description: CRITICAL/HIGH counts AS SCANNED, per severity. Meaningful only together with evidence_class and package_inventory_source.kind.

findings_by_package.description: Optional per-package finding counts. Present in the base-vs-child regression fixture because linux-libc-dev is the package that makes the two classes visibly different.

staging_package.description: Required in practice for staged-candidate: the package the candidate was pushed to.

release_identity.description: Required in practice for published-artifact: the release version it was published under.
